title: Reprendre un lieu, un complément ou une idée
summary: Choose `y`, `en` or neutral `le` by the construction being replaced, not by an English word.
objectives: Replace suitable `à` and `de` phrases with `y` and `en`.
Use neutral `le` for an idea or an adjective without agreement.
Place the pronoun with the verb it belongs to.

sources.label: University of Texas: pronoun order and negation
B1 public topic index (coverage reference only)
OQLF: en, including references to people
Le Robert: penser à and its personal complements

sections.title: `Y` replaces a location or a suitable `à` + thing phrase
paragraphs: `Y` can replace a place introduced by `à`, `dans`, `chez` and other location expressions when the meaning is there: `Je travaille dans ce bâtiment` becomes `J'y travaille`. It also replaces `à` + a thing or idea after verbs that take that construction: `penser à ce problème` becomes `y penser`.

Do not replace every `à` phrase with `y`. For people, `parler à Léa` becomes `lui parler`, while `penser à Léa` normally becomes `penser à elle`. The verb's construction determines the pronoun. `Y` is not the standard replacement for a named person in the contrasts taught here.
points: Vocabulary: `une proposition` (feminine), a proposal; `un bâtiment` (masculine), a building.
A destination need not be physically close for `y` to be possible.

examples.french: Je travaille dans ce bâtiment. J'**y** travaille depuis juin.
examples.english: I work in this building. I have been working there since June.

examples.french: Tu penses à cette proposition? Tu **y** penses vraiment?
examples.english: Are you thinking about this proposal? Are you really thinking about it?

examples.french: Je pense à Nora. Je pense **à elle**.
examples.english: I am thinking about Nora. I am thinking about her.
examples.note: Use a stressed person pronoun with `penser à`.

mistakes.avoid: Je pense ce projet. J'y pense.
mistakes.prefer: Je pense à ce projet. J'y pense.
mistakes.why: `Y` preserves an underlying `à` construction; it does not make `penser` into a direct-object verb.

sections.title: `En` replaces a `de` phrase or a quantity noun
paragraphs: `En` replaces `de` + a thing or idea after a verb or adjective: `parler de ce projet` becomes `en parler`; `être fier de son travail` becomes `en être fier`. It can also replace an origin: `revenir de Lyon` becomes `en revenir`. A quantity word or number stays outside `en`: `J'ai trois billets` becomes `J'en ai trois`.

For people, `de lui/d'elle/d'eux/d'elles` is often clearer and is the form practiced when emphasizing the person. `En` can refer to people in some constructions and registers, so it is not universally forbidden. Compare quantity `J'ai deux sœurs, j'en ai deux`, which is normal.
points: With a negative quantity, use `Je n'en ai pas`; do not keep `un` just because English says one unless the exact count is being contrasted.
A `de` phrase that belongs to a noun or is part of a fixed expression needs its own construction analysis; do not delete every occurrence of `de` automatically.

examples.french: Nous parlons du budget. Nous **en** parlons demain.
examples.english: We are talking about the budget. We will talk about it tomorrow.
examples.note: `Du` is `de + le`, and `en` replaces the complete phrase.

examples.french: Elle est fière de son travail. Elle **en** est fière.
examples.english: She is proud of her work. She is proud of it.
examples.note: `En` can replace the complement of an adjective.

examples.french: Vous avez trois billets? Oui, nous **en** avons trois.
examples.english: Do you have three tickets? Yes, we have three.
examples.note: Keep the number after the verb.

mistakes.prefer: J'ai deux billets. J'en ai deux.
mistakes.why: To preserve the exact stated quantity, keep `deux`. `J'en ai` alone only says I have some.

sections.title: `Le` can stand for a whole idea or a description
paragraphs: Neutral `le` refers to a statement or idea, not a masculine noun: `Il est parti, je le sais` means I know that he has left. It becomes `l'` before a vowel. Unlike an ordinary direct-object pronoun replacing a noun, this neutral `le` does not change to `la` or `les`.

After verbs such as `être`, `le` can replace a previously mentioned adjective or description: `Elle est prête, je le suis aussi`. `Le` remains neutral even if the speaker is a woman or several people are described. A following `avoir` participle is likewise not made feminine or plural merely because the idea concerns women.
points: Compare `Les clés? Je les ai` (a plural noun) with `Elles sont parties? Je le sais` (a whole statement).
Place pronouns before the finite verb or compound auxiliary: `je l'ai compris`. With an infinitive, place the pronoun before the infinitive it belongs to: `je vais y réfléchir`; `je veux en parler`.

examples.french: La réunion est annulée. Je **le** sais.
examples.english: The meeting is cancelled. I know that.
examples.note: `Le` replaces the whole fact, not the feminine noun `réunion`.

examples.french: Tu savais qu'elle viendrait? Oui, je **l'**avais compris.
examples.english: Did you know she would come? Yes, I had understood that.

examples.french: Elles sont prêtes, et nous **le** sommes aussi.
examples.english: They are ready, and so are we.

examples.french: Cette question est importante; je vais **y** réfléchir.
examples.english: This question is important; I am going to think about it.
examples.note: `Y` belongs to `réfléchir à`, so it sits before `réfléchir`.

sections.title: Rétablir le complément entier avant de choisir
paragraphs: A pronoun can replace an action as well as an object. Rebuild the full complement: `renoncer à modifier le plan` gives `y renoncer`, because `à` introduces the action. By contrast, a previously mentioned action can be recalled with `le faire` when `faire` means do that. The presence of an infinitive in the original is not by itself a reason to choose `y`.

Also distinguish an unspecified amount from an identified object. `Du tissu`, some fabric, can become `en`; `ce tissu`, this particular fabric, can become `le`. The fact that fabric is a mass substance does not force `en` when the original phrase identifies it as a whole. With quantities of people, `en` is ordinary too: it can stand for the counted noun while a number remains. A blanket ban on `en` referring to people would be wrong.

Use a three-step check: restore the missing words, locate any preposition required by the original construction, and keep any quantity or description that the pronoun does not replace. Then put the pronoun beside the verb it belongs to. For a person after `penser à`, keep `à` plus the stressed pronoun; do not assume that every person introduced by `à` becomes `lui` or `leur`.
points: Vocabulary: `le tissu` (masculine), fabric; `un interprète / une interprète` (masculine/feminine), an interpreter.

examples.french: Renoncer à modifier le plan ? Nous **y renoncerons** seulement si c'est nécessaire.
examples.english: Give up changing the plan? We will give that up only if necessary.

examples.french: Reprendre les mesures ? Nous pouvons **le faire** maintenant.
examples.english: Take the measurements again? We can do that now.
examples.note: `Le faire` recalls the action as a whole.

examples.french: Du tissu, j'**en** coupe pour les essais. Ce tissu épais, je **le** garde pour les sacs.
examples.english: I cut some fabric for the trials. I keep this thick fabric for the bags.
examples.note: An amount and a particular identified material have different references.

examples.english: The team is looking for two interpreters.
examples.note: `En` can refer to people in a quantity construction; `deux` remains.

practice.prompt: Replace à cette question with y: Nous réfléchissons à cette question.
practice.explanation: Réfléchir à a thing allows y.

practice.prompt: Replace de ce problème with en: Elle parle de ce problème.
practice.explanation: En replaces the de complement.

practice.prompt: Supply le, la or les for the fact: La porte est fermée; je ___ sais.
practice.explanation: The pronoun replaces the statement, not porte.

practice.prompt: Supply the neutral pronoun: Elles sont patientes; vous ___ êtes aussi.
practice.explanation: Neutral le replaces the adjective and elides before êtes.

practice.prompt: Replace dans cette salle with y: Les stagiaires travaillent dans cette salle.
practice.explanation: Y replaces a location introduced by dans.

practice.prompt: Replace du résultat with en: Nous sommes satisfaits du résultat.
practice.explanation: En replaces the adjective's de complement.

practice.prompt: Replace the noun billets with en while preserving the exact quantity: J'ai quatre billets.
practice.explanation: Keep quatre after the verb.

practice.prompt: Supply le, la or les for the whole fact: Elles ont gagné; nous ___ savons.
practice.explanation: A whole fact takes neutral le.

practice.prompt: Supply le, la or les: Ma sœur est prête; je ___ suis aussi. The speaker is a woman.
practice.explanation: Neutral le does not agree with the female speaker or adjective.

practice.prompt: Replace à ce projet with y: Je vais réfléchir à ce projet.
practice.explanation: Y belongs before the infinitive réfléchir.

practice.prompt: Replace de cette difficulté with en: Nous voulons parler de cette difficulté.
practice.explanation: En belongs to parler, not vouloir.

practice.prompt: Choose the standard replacement emphasizing the person in Je pense à Sami.
practice.explanation: Use a stressed person pronoun with penser à in this contrast.

practice.prompt: Replace de Bordeaux with en: Elle revient de Bordeaux.
practice.explanation: En can replace an origin introduced by de.

practice.prompt: Replace au rendez-vous with y: Je ne suis pas allé au rendez-vous.
practice.explanation: Y precedes the auxiliary inside the negative group.

practice.prompt: Supply the neutral pronoun before ai: C'était une erreur; je ___ ai compris trop tard.
practice.explanation: Neutral le elides before ai and replaces the fact.

practice.prompt: Supply the neutral pronoun: Ils sont disponibles; nous ___ serons demain.
practice.explanation: Le replaces the adjective regardless of plural subjects.

practice.prompt: Replace the whole phrase à changer d'horaire with y, keeping the other words: Nous songeons à changer d'horaire.
practice.explanation: Songer à takes an à complement, here an action. Y replaces that whole complement.

practice.prompt: Avoid repeating vérifier les données by using the taught two-word group le + faire: Vérifier les données ? Je vais ___ après la pause.
practice.explanation: Neutral le with faire recalls the action; it goes before the infinitive faire.

practice.prompt: Replace the specifically identified la farine in this sentence with a direct-object pronoun, without changing anything else: Je pèse la farine.
practice.explanation: The definite feminine noun phrase refers to the identified flour, so la is appropriate rather than a pronoun meaning some of it.

practice.prompt: Replace assistants with en and preserve the number: Nous recrutons trois assistants.
practice.explanation: En can replace a counted noun referring to people; keep trois.

production_task.prompt: Write a short exchange about a proposed workshop. Mention the location and return to it with `y`; mention a topic with `de` and return to it with `en`; confirm a whole fact with `le`; use neutral `le` for an adjective.
production_task.model_answer: L'atelier aura lieu à la mairie. Nous y irons samedi. Nous devons parler du budget; nous en parlerons après la visite. La salle est petite, je le sais. Les bénévoles sont motivés, et je le suis aussi.
production_task.translation: The workshop will take place at the town hall. We will go there on Saturday. We need to talk about the budget; we will discuss it after the visit. The room is small, I know that. The volunteers are motivated, and so am I.
rubric: Distinguish a `de` complement, a location and a whole fact.
Do not make neutral `le` agree with an adjective or subject.
Place the pronoun with the appropriate verb.
